conversation.content:
Good morning—thank you for making time today. I’m Claire, a perinatal mental-health clinician. Over the next few minutes I’d like to use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. This is simply a routine screen for mood and anxiety symptoms that can crop up in the first year postpartum; it isn’t a test you can pass or fail, and every answer is confidential between you and our team. We’ll walk through ten short questions about the past seven days. When you’re ready, we can start with the first one:

In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?
Good morning. Yeah, I can still laugh—just not as easily as before. Like, if my partner jokes around I’ll smile, but it doesn’t feel as natural or last as long.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I’ve been able to laugh, but it feels kind of forced. Most of the time I’m just tired, so even when something’s funny, I don’t get that same light feeling I used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
I do look forward to some things—like my mom coming over or getting out for a short walk—but the excitement isn’t as big as it used to be. It’s more “that’ll be nice” than really feeling pumped.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Yesterday the baby was fussy and I kept thinking maybe I’m not feeding him right or holding him the “best” way. I know it’s probably not rational, but the thought still pops up.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason
Sometimes I do get that jittery feeling out of nowhere—like I’ll suddenly worry that the baby’s too quiet or that I missed something important. It usually passes pretty quickly, but yeah, it happens.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
Not really panicked—more like a quick flutter of “what if something’s wrong?” and then I can calm myself. It’s not the full-blown scared feeling, just a brief spike that settles once I check on him.
Things have been getting on top of me

A little bit, yeah. Some days the diapers and feedings just feel endless, and I think, “How am I going to get through tomorrow?” It’s not every moment, but when the fatigue hits, it can feel like too much.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, I can still fall asleep—sometimes it just takes me longer if I’m replaying the day in my head, but once I’m out I stay asleep. It’s more tiredness than unhappiness keeping me awake.
I have felt sad or miserable
Yeah, I’ve had moments of feeling sad—like a heaviness that shows up for no clear reason. It’s not all day, but a few evenings this week I just felt kind of down and weepy.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
I’ve cried a couple of times—mostly when I’m worn out and everything feels a little overwhelming. It’s not constant, just a release when the stress piles up.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, that hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 13: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother, infant age not specified  
Date: [today’s date]  
Screener: [name, credentials]

Symptoms endorsed  
- Anhedonia/lack of pleasure: laughter feels forced; diminished anticipatory enjoyment  
- Depressed mood: intermittent sadness, “heaviness,” tearfulness several evenings/week  
- Excessive guilt/self-blame: questions own caregiving adequacy despite objective safety  
- Anxiety: unexpected jittery/worried spikes, brief “what-if” cognitions, no panic attacks  
- Feeling overwhelmed/fatigue: chores feel “endless,” anticipatory dread of next day  
- Mild sleep-onset delay related to rumination, no middle/late insomnia or self-harm thoughts

Pattern  
Mild–moderate depressive and anxious symptoms occurring “some days,” worse with fatigue, no current safety concerns.

Risk indicators  
- Persistent low mood and crying spells  
- Reduced pleasure in previously enjoyable activities  
- Maladaptive guilt/cognitive self-criticism  
- Situational anxiety without clear precipitant  
- Denies suicidal or homicidal ideation (documented safety screen negative)

Screening impression  
Meets partial criteria for postpartum depression and anxiety; severity appears subthreshold but clinically significant. Recommend formal evaluation (EPDS score, clinical interview) and monitoring for escalation.
